source.quote: Luckily, we've already pushed our skill up to 300 classic fishing, so there's no leveling grinding needed. And in Swamp of Sorrows, there's two main ways to fish for gold, and today we're testing both to see which one comes out on top. Now, the first option is fishing directly from pools and schools, and these are mostly stone scale eel swarms out here, and the loot table isn't too exciting. The stone scale eels selling for only one gold and 66 silver each. But, these pools do have a chance to drop mithril-bound trunks. There isn't a confirmed drop rate on Wowhead, but it seems to be somewhere around 5%. Now, the trunks themselves can contain a mix of green BOEs and recipes, a bit of the RNG loot piñata. Now, we can also find floating wreckage pools that spawn in the same locations as the eels. They're rare spawns, so to get them to appear, we'll need to clear all of the eel pools. The wreckage pools drop them at a much higher rate, and they also add iron lockboxes to the mix. So, the pool method is definitely a loot box opening angle. So, to get a fair in the numbers, let's go ahead and farm for 1 hour, see how many mithril lockboxes we can gather up, and see what kind of loot is hiding inside of them.

source.quote: All right, and here's the haul. 27 mithril-bound trunks, and two iron-bound trunks. Now, of course, while fishing I also snagged a couple of coastal rare spawns that totaled in about 2,200 gold in item value. And the raw fish of the eels is worth a solid few hundred gold, putting the pre-box opening value at 2,640 gold. Of course, the 2,200 gold from rares is pretty random, and there may or may not be a rare spawn when we fish this every time, but today we got it. But, onto the boxes. And at first, it's nothing special, but about halfway through, check this out. The glyphed apaulets, a leather shoulder worth about 2,500 gold. And not too far along after, the black forge girdle, clocking in at about 964 gold. Now, the rest of the boxes just have some trade goods, some leather, and some cloth, but in total, we pulled in 4,200 gold from the 29 boxes, giving us an average box value of about 149 gold each. And that puts our net gold per hour for the pool farm at 6.8 thousand gold, which really isn't bad. But, keep in mind, about 5,000 of that is transmog value, which will sell slower, and the remaining 1.8 thousand does come from fish and leather and miscellaneous trade goods. So, it's a pretty decent dual farm. But, like I said, we still need to test open water fishing, because there are some big fish available here. But first, let's talk about the sponsor for our video today, AG1. And to best do that, let's pop into IRL.

source.quote: But, the best chance to get heavy hides is actually with skinning level 175 to 205, and particularly from skinning dragonkin. So, here's the experiment. If we reset skinning from 300 back down to level one, and re-level it inside the dungeon farming the Sunken Temple, we'll naturally pass through that sweet spot of 175 to 205. The question is, will we pick up any extra heavy hides, and will this offset the lost value from farming through all those early scraps of light leathers and rugged leather scraps? Well, let's find out. Of course, leather isn't the only thing on the menu here, and the real Sunken Temple prize are rare BOE weapons. And there is about eight unique drops. Now, we talked about Death Blow and Stealth Blade last episode, which are two of the cooler ones, but there's also Ragehammer, a two-handed mace worth around 209,000 gold. Then, there's the Bludgeon of the Grinning Dog, a staff worth about 120,000 gold. And also, I kind of just want to know which dev named the items in Sunken Temple, because these names are wild. But anyways, there's also the Stinging Bow coming in at around 78,000 gold, though its appearance isn't anything that special. And Winter's Bite, a one-handed axe with a massive 250,000 gold price tag. Now, of course, they're all insanely rare, but just one of these would be a huge win for the transmog shelves. So, after an hour of testing, here's how it shook out. Running from one to 300 skinning in the dungeon, we ended up with almost every kind of hide in the game, including five heavy hides, which is, of course, always welcomed.

source.quote: Now, in this zone, there's a few things going on. There's festivities, quests, but a big-ticket one is event vendors, and they offer transmog and cosmetics in exchange for the event currency, Tricky Treats. But, we're not here for transmog, because everything they sell here is soulbound and can't be sold in the auction house, at least for transmog. We're after valuable items and quality-of-life upgrades. And to get them, we're going to need to maximize our trick-or-treating and daily quests, since we're going to be limited to what zones we currently have unlocked. Now, looking at the vendors, the first prize worth mentioning is the Magic Broom. It does cost 50 Tricky Treats, which is pretty low, and acts as an instant-cast flying mount. And with the mining while mounted bug patched, this is about as close as Goldie will get back to it. And this instant-cast mount could save us serious time on gathering runs without having to hard-cast mount after every single node. But, the downside is it's only available during Hallow's End. So, when the event ends on midnight, November 1st, the broom would disappear as well. But, something a little more permanent is the Headless Horseman's Hearthstone. This toy would allow us to delete our actual Hearthstone, freeing up an extra bag slot, which, as you know, are always precious.

records.summary: 377 Thorium,10 Crystals,77 Thick Leather,20 Rugged,99 Scales,35 Meat,46 Clams;8100 gmaterials atlowerprices plus 5500 transmog=13600 valuation. Aegis Stormwind, Dark Phantom Cape, Champions Chestplate drops.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/013 - Swamp of Sorrows Is A GRIND... Can I Escape Today？ - Goldbound Episode 13.en-orig.txt
source.quote: But, it got me thinking. What if we planned something a little more efficient? A farm that could min-max this downtime? And really, what would be a better filler than the turtle farm? So, here's the plan. From turtles alone, we know we can pull about 8,300 gold per hour, and mining on its own came in lower at about 6,700 gold per hour. So, the idea is to do one loop of zone mining, and then farm turtles for 3 to 5 minutes. This should let the thorium nodes respawn, and then we can loop it again. The question is, could this hybrid method outpace both farms? Now, of course, the route itself is straightforward, a circle of the zone and clearing the turtle camps. But, I also made sure to dip into the cave on every run, since it actually holds four to six thorium spawns along with a few mobs. And as a bonus, I think these loops might actually reset some of the open-world loot bugs, which means we might actually see some transmog dropping from the cave dwellers and the turtles. So, after an hour of testing, what are the results? And firstly, our suspicion of the bugged loot seemed to be correct, because we pulled in a few transmog items. First up, the Aegis of Stormwind. This is a blue BoE shield worth about 2,000 gold, but with its appearance, a piece you could easily see players buying. We also got the Dark Phantom Cape. This is a 3,000 gold cloak, and it being a full-length cloak actually looks pretty darn good. Now, we also got a handful of greens, but the only one we're actually going to list and sell is the Champion's Chestplate, worth just around 1,500 gold. So, that's about 5.5 thousand gold in transmog value, which really isn't bad, although it is variable. So, let's focus in on the direct trade goods, since those are a little more consistent. Now, for mining in this hour, we actually got 377 thorium ore, which is more than we got in the pure mining test, which is crazy considering how much time we actually also spent killing turtles. But, prices on thorium ore have dropped since our last video, from 10 to 11 gold each down to about 7 to 8 gold each. But, we still have about 3,000 gold total just from thorium. And for arcane crystals, we still snagged 10, selling at around 267 gold each for another 2,670 gold. That's close to our previous rate, where we got 12 before, but the prices are also a bit lower than last time.

Think it's worth noting that one thing we haven't really leaned into this zone is rare spawn hunting. And it's not that the Swamp of Sorrows is a lack of rares. There's actually 16 of them. The issue is that none of them actually stand out the way Mother Fang, Fedfennel, or Ro the Silent did. There just aren't any rares here that drop insanely valuable single ticket items. That said, they're still worth killing because many of the rares carry 500 to 2,000 gold transmog pieces. It's just that they're like Snarlflare in Redridge. You take them down if you see them, but they're not really worth camping or timing their spawns for.
